title: Death notice definition: what it is and how to write one
excerpt: Learn what a death notice is and how to write one effectively to inform your community about a passing in a clear and respectful way.
content:
![Hands placing death notice in newspaper](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787057004128_Hands-placing-death-notice-in-newspaper.jpeg)

A death notice is a short, factual announcement that someone has died, giving the name, age and immediate family so the community can be informed quickly. It differs from an obituary, which is a longer tribute telling the story of a person's [life and legacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obituary). Families often place a notice within [two to four days of a death](https://yurn.com.au/how-to-write-a-funeral-notice/), through a source such as Willow Tree Funerals or a newspaper's announcements page, well before the fuller obituary follows.

## Key Takeaways

A death notice is a brief, factual passing announcement, while an obituary is a longer life tribute published separately, often days later.

| Point | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Definition first | A death notice states name, age, date of death and immediate family, nothing more required. |
| Not the same as an obituary | Obituaries tell a life story; death notices simply announce the passing. |
| Timing matters | Print notices typically go out within two to four days, ahead of a service held within the week. |
| Publication is custom, not law | Nothing legally forces publication anywhere in Australia; etiquette and family wishes guide the decision. |
| Funeral directors can handle it | Willow Tree Funerals drafts, confirms and submits notices as part of standard funeral arrangement. |

## Table of Contents

- [What is a death notice, and why do families use one?](#what-is-a-death-notice-and-why-do-families-use-one)
- [Death notice vs funeral notice vs obituary: which one do you need?](#death-notice-vs-funeral-notice-vs-obituary-which-one-do-you-need)
- [What to include and how to write it (with an example)](#what-to-include-and-how-to-write-it-with-an-example)
- [Where to publish a death notice and what it typically costs](#where-to-publish-a-death-notice-and-what-it-typically-costs)
- [Do you have to publish one, and what does etiquette require?](#do-you-have-to-publish-one-and-what-does-etiquette-require)
- [How a funeral director helps place a death notice](#how-a-funeral-director-helps-place-a-death-notice)
- [Why families overthink death notices more than they need to](#why-families-overthink-death-notices-more-than-they-need-to)
- [Sources](#sources)
- [FAQ](#faq)

## What is a death notice, and why do families use one?

A death notice exists to do one job well: tell people, quickly and plainly, that a death has occurred. It names the deceased, usually gives their age, states the date of death, and names the immediate family left behind. Some notices add a line about a service; many do not.

![Death notice example in newspaper page](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787057002810_Death-notice-example-in-newspaper-page.jpeg)

Families and funeral directors write and place these notices, and they choose a short notice over a lengthy tribute for a simple reason: speed matters more than eloquence in the first few days after a loss. A death notice reaches the wider community while grief is still raw and decisions are still being made.

You'll typically see them in:

- Print newspaper birth, marriage and death (BMD) pages
- Funeral home websites, including dedicated obituary pages
- Notice aggregator sites that compile listings from multiple funeral homes
- Social media posts from family members
- Email chains to extended family, colleagues, or community groups

## Death notice vs funeral notice vs obituary: which one do you need?

These three terms get used loosely, but each one does a distinct job. A death notice announces that someone has passed. A funeral notice carries the same short format but adds the specifics of the service, the time, date and venue, effectively turning an announcement into an invitation. An obituary is different in kind, not just length: it tells the story of who someone was, not just that they died.

- **Death notice**: name, age, date of death, immediate family. Nothing more required.
- **Funeral notice**: everything in a death notice, plus service details, [typically running under 150 words](https://foreverinourhearts.com.au/funeral-notices-in-australia-what-to-include-and-where-to-post) because newspapers charge by the line.
- **Obituary**: a full account of a life, published in print, online, or both, often days or weeks later.

Families commonly publish a death or funeral notice first, then follow with a fuller obituary once there's time to write it properly. The most common mistake is assuming a death notice must carry service information. It doesn't. Plenty of families deliberately keep the notice minimal and share service details privately with close contacts instead.

## What to include and how to write it (with an example)

A workable death notice needs surprisingly little: the full name, age, date of death, immediate family members, and either a brief service note or the word "private" if the family isn't inviting broader attendance. Add a donation request or livestream link only if it's genuinely relevant.

Three templates cover most situations:

- **Single-line public notice**: "[Full name], aged [age], of [suburb], passed away peacefully on [date]. Loved husband/wife of [name], father/mother of [names]."
- **Family notice**: adds a line naming grandchildren, siblings, or extended family, and a short phrase like "forever in our hearts."
- **Funeral notice**: everything above, plus "Funeral service to be held at [venue], [date] at [time]. All welcome" or "Private family service."

A filled example: "Margaret Anne Wilson, aged 84, of Hurstville, passed away peacefully on 3 March 2026. Beloved wife of the late Frank, loving mother of Susan and David. Funeral Mass at St Joseph's Catholic Church, Hurstville, Friday 7 March at 10:00am. All welcome."

**Pro Tip:** *Draft the notice, then read it aloud before sending it anywhere. Wrong dates and misspelled names are the two errors that cause the most distress once a notice is in print and can't be unpublished.*

![Hands typing notice draft by candlelight](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787057028524_Hands-typing-notice-draft-by-candlelight.jpeg)

Avoid cramming in unnecessary detail. A notice isn't the place for the full life story; save that for the obituary.

## Where to publish a death notice and what it typically costs

Print newspapers remain the traditional channel for death notices, particularly for older or regional communities who still check the BMD pages out of habit. Funeral home websites and notice aggregator sites have become just as common, and [notices increasingly appear online as well as in print](https://ezifunerals.com.au/death-funeral-notices/), reaching family and friends who've moved interstate or overseas.

For timing, aim to publish within a few days of the death if you're using print, since services often follow soon and you want the community informed beforehand. Online notices can go up faster and stay accessible indefinitely, which is why many families use both.

- Newspapers charge by the line or column centimetre, so cost scales with length. This is exactly why printed notices stay short and full obituaries move online.
- Funeral-home websites and aggregator listings are often included in the service, or cost far less than equivalent newspaper space.
- Social media and email cost nothing but reach a narrower, self-selected audience.
- A family member or a funeral director such as Willow Tree Funerals can place the notice on the family's behalf.

## Do you have to publish one, and what does etiquette require?

Publishing a death notice is rarely a legal requirement anywhere in Australia. It's a matter of custom and courtesy, not law, though it's worth checking specific state or council requirements if you're unsure. What matters more is getting the tone and detail right.

- Keep the wording factual, warm and respectful. Avoid florid language that obscures the basic facts.
- Double check names, dates and titles before submission. Errors in a published notice are hard to correct.
- Be mindful of privacy and cultural or religious practice, particularly around cause of death.
- Use "private service" or "no flowers by request" clearly if that reflects the family's wishes.

The most common pitfall is posting sensitive detail to social media before the wider family has been told directly.

## How a funeral director helps place a death notice

A funeral director takes the pressure off a family already stretched thin. Willow Tree Funerals, for one, treats notice drafting as a standard part of arranging a service rather than an optional extra.

1. Draft the wording with the family, checking names, dates and relationships carefully.
2. Confirm service date, time and venue before anything is submitted.
3. Liaise directly with the newspaper on deadlines and formatting.
4. Arrange the matching online notice, usually published on the funeral home's own site.
5. Send a proof copy back to the family for final approval before it runs.

Expect a modest fee for this drafting and placement work, on top of any newspaper line charges, and Willow Tree Funerals lists [funeral pricing openly](https://willowtreefunerals.com.au/pricing) so there are no surprises.

**Pro Tip:** *If family members are scattered across time zones, ask the funeral director to circulate the draft by email before submission. It avoids last-minute disputes over wording when someone overseas sees the notice for the first time after it's already published.*

## Why families overthink death notices more than they need to

The conventional advice on this topic tends to treat wording as the hard part. It isn't. The hard part is deciding, early and clearly, what belongs in the immediate notice and what waits for the obituary. Families who blur that line end up either publishing too little too late, or crowding a notice with detail that belongs in a proper tribute.

![Comparison diagram of death notice and obituary](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787057047337_Comparison-diagram-of-death-notice-and-obituary.jpeg)

My view, shaped by seeing this play out repeatedly: get the short notice out fast, keep it strictly factual, and give yourself permission to write the obituary later, when there's actually room to do the person justice. Don't let a newspaper deadline force you into writing a eulogy on day one. A death notice's whole value is speed and clarity, not completeness. If a funeral director is handling arrangements, let them draft the notice while you focus on the parts of this that a template can't help with.

## Sources

For background on the format, see Wikipedia's entry on obituaries. For Australian-specific templates and examples, Willow Tree Funerals' obituary page and [blog resources](https://willowtreefunerals.com.au/blog) cover practical wording and process.

- Obituary — Wikipedia

## FAQ

### What counts as a death notice?

A death notice is a short, factual announcement naming the deceased, their age, date of death and immediate family, published to inform the community quickly.

### What is the difference between a death notice and an obituary?

A death notice is a brief announcement of a passing, while an obituary is a longer piece describing a person's life and legacy, usually published separately.

### What is an example of a death notice?

A typical example reads: "Margaret Anne Wilson, aged 84, of Hurstville, passed away peacefully on 3 March 2026. Beloved wife of the late Frank, loving mother of Susan and David."

### Do you have to put a death notice in the paper in Australia?

No. Publishing a death notice is a matter of custom rather than legal requirement, though it's worth checking any specific state or council rules if you're uncertain.

title: What happens to tenancy in common death: your estate guide
excerpt: When a co-owner dies in a tenancy in common, their share belongs to their estate. Learn how this affects inheritance and avoid disputes.
content:
![Hands examining property title document](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787057007209_Hands-examining-property-title-document.jpeg)

When a co-owner dies, their share in a tenancy in common does not pass automatically to the other owners. It becomes part of their deceased estate, distributed under their Will or, if there is no valid Will, under intestacy law. State and territory processes vary, and a grant of probate or letters of administration is usually required before that share can change hands.

- No right of survivorship exists for tenants in common.
- The deceased's share is an estate asset, not a gift to co-owners.
- Distribution follows the Will, or intestacy rules where none exists.

## Key Takeaways

A tenant in common's share always passes through their estate rather than automatically to co-owners, making probate, transmission paperwork, and executor duties unavoidable steps.

| Point | Details |
| --- | --- |
| No automatic transfer | A deceased tenant in common's share becomes part of their estate, not the co-owner's property. |
| Probate usually required | Executors typically need a grant of probate or letters of administration before transferring title. |
| Document trail matters | Death certificate, Will, grant, registrar's certificate, and transmission form are all commonly required. |
| Multiple exit options exist | Surviving co-owners can buy out, sell, keep co-owning, or apply for court partition. |
| Tax questions need specialist help | CGT on inherited shares depends on acquisition history, so involve a tax adviser before selling. |

## Table of Contents

- [Tenancy in common vs joint tenancy: why it matters when someone dies](#tenancy-in-common-vs-joint-tenancy-why-it-matters-when-someone-dies)
- [What happens legally to a deceased tenant in common's share](#what-happens-legally-to-a-deceased-tenant-in-commons-share)
- [What steps should executors and co-owners take first?](#what-steps-should-executors-and-co-owners-take-first)
- [What are the options for surviving co-owners?](#what-are-the-options-for-surviving-co-owners)
- [Does the ATO tax an inherited tenancy in common share?](#does-the-ato-tax-an-inherited-tenancy-in-common-share)
- [How long does transferring the title take, and what does it cost?](#how-long-does-transferring-the-title-take-and-what-does-it-cost)
- [When should you call a lawyer or tax adviser?](#when-should-you-call-a-lawyer-or-tax-adviser)
- [Where to check the official rules next](#where-to-check-the-official-rules-next)
- [A funeral director's view on tenancy in common death](#a-funeral-directors-view-on-tenancy-in-common-death)
- [Sources](#sources)
- [FAQ](#faq)

## Tenancy in common vs joint tenancy: why it matters when someone dies

The ownership structure chosen at settlement decides who inherits when a co-owner dies. Get this wrong at the outset and a family can end up in years of dispute.

**Tenants in common** hold defined shares, which can be equal or unequal, and each share [forms part of the deceased estate](https://www.aussie.com.au/insights/articles/joint-tenants-tenants-in-common-difference/) rather than transferring automatically. **Joint tenants** hold equal, undivided interests with a right of survivorship, so a deceased owner's interest passes directly to the surviving joint tenant, bypassing the estate entirely.

| Feature | Tenants in common | Joint tenants |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Share size | Equal or unequal, defined | Always equal |
| On death | Passes via Will or intestacy | Passes to surviving owner automatically |
| Estate involvement | Yes, requires probate/administration | No, avoids probate for that asset |

Consider a blended family where a parent holds a majority share and an adult child holds a minority share as tenants in common. On the parent's death, that majority share goes wherever their Will directs, perhaps split between step-children, rather than automatically consolidating with the co-owner.

- Tenants in common: your share is yours to leave to whomever you choose.
- Joint tenants: the last owner standing takes the whole property.

## What happens legally to a deceased tenant in common's share

The [share becomes an asset of the deceased estate](https://hqf.com.au/what-happens-to-property-when-co-owner-dies/), sitting alongside bank accounts, superannuation, and other property until the executor deals with it. Surviving co-owners have no automatic claim, no matter how long they lived in the property or how the mortgage was split.

An executor named in the Will, or an administrator appointed under intestacy, must apply for a grant of probate or letters of administration before the title can move. Land titles offices then require a [transmission application supported by the registrar's certificate](https://www.landservices.com.au/land-registration/change-ownership-following-a-death/), evidence of the grant, and identity verification for whoever is lodging the paperwork.

- The share does not transfer to co-owners by default.
- Probate or letters of administration is typically the first legal gate.
- A transmission application registers the change of ownership on title.
- Any mortgage or secured debt remains the estate's responsibility until settled.

**Pro Tip:** *Order a fresh title search the moment you're appointed executor. It confirms exactly how the property is held and stops nasty surprises months into administration.*

## What steps should executors and co-owners take first?

Handling a co-owned property after a death follows a fairly predictable sequence, even though paperwork differs slightly between registries.

1. Confirm the ownership structure by pulling a title search: tenants in common or joint tenancy.
2. Locate the original Will and obtain the death certificate.
3. Notify the mortgagee and the property insurer of the death.
4. Contact the probate registry in the deceased's state or territory to begin the application.
5. Once granted, lodge the transmission application with the relevant land titles office.

The document trail matters as much as the sequence. You will typically need:

- Original death certificate
- The Will (or evidence of intestacy)
- Grant of probate or letters of administration
- Registrar's certificate
- Completed transmission application form
- Identity verification documents for the applicant

Registries [differ in their exact forms and verification standards](https://www.land.vic.gov.au/land-registration/fees-guides-and-forms), so check the specific requirements for the state where the property sits before lodging anything. Self-represented executors can lodge these forms directly in straightforward estates, but a conveyancer or solicitor earns their fee quickly once a mortgage discharge, a contested Will, or an interstate asset enters the picture. Gathering your documents early, including the paperwork families often assemble for other estate matters, saves weeks later.

## What are the options for surviving co-owners?

Once the deceased's share sits with beneficiaries, everyone involved faces a genuine choice, and the right answer depends on finances as much as family harmony.

- **The surviving co-owner buys the beneficiary out.** This keeps the property in familiar hands but requires a valuation and, often, refinancing to release funds.
- **Sell the property and split the proceeds.** Cleanest option when no one wants to keep the asset, though it needs agreement from all owners and can take months in a slow market.
- **Continue as co-owners with new parties.** Beneficiaries step into the deceased's share, which works if relationships are strong but risks friction over maintenance costs and decision-making.
- **Apply to the court for partition or sale.** A last resort when co-owners cannot agree, [involving valuation, mortgage consent, and formal orders](https://sunstateconveyancing.com.au/joint-property-in-australia-understanding-tenants-in-common-and-what-happens-upon-death/) that add cost and delay.

Each path needs mortgage consent from the lender, an independent valuation, and correctly drafted transfer forms before title changes hands.

## Does the ATO tax an inherited tenancy in common share?

Capital gains tax is the question every beneficiary eventually asks, and the answer depends on how the property was used and when it was acquired.

> The ATO confirms that when a tenant in common dies, their share does not pass by survivorship. It forms part of the deceased's estate and is [subject to the inherited assets and CGT rules](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/inherited-assets-and-capital-gains-tax/co-ownership-and-right-of-survivorship) that apply to estate assets generally.

A CGT event typically arises later, when the inherited share is eventually sold rather than at the moment of inheritance. Whether the main residence exemption applies depends on how long the deceased lived there and how quickly beneficiaries deal with the property, details specific enough that a general rule rarely fits every family.

**Pro Tip:** *Get a tax adviser involved before signing any sale contract on an inherited share. CGT calculations on inherited property hinge on acquisition dates and use history that are easy to get wrong without records in hand.*

## How long does transferring the title take, and what does it cost?

Timeframes swing widely. A straightforward, uncontested estate with a valid Will can see probate granted within a few weeks in some registries, while contested estates or court backlogs stretch this out considerably. Costs stack up from several directions rather than one flat fee.

- Probate or letters of administration application fees, which vary by state and estate value.
- Land titles transmission and registration fees for the title change itself.
- Solicitor or conveyancer fees for handling the paperwork.
- Property valuation costs, often required for CGT and buy-out calculations.

Contested Wills, unresolved mortgages, and assets spread across more than one state all push both timing and cost upward.

## When should you call a lawyer or tax adviser?

Some estates run smoothly with an executor handling paperwork solo. Others need professional help fast, and knowing which category you're in saves money and stress.

> Practical experience from conveyancing practices shows that failing to check the title early is one of the most common causes of dispute and delay, leaving surviving partners unexpectedly co-owning with beneficiaries they never expected to deal with.

Watch for these signals: unclear ownership recorded on title, a contested Will or a claim against the estate, disputes with a mortgagee or creditor, assets spread across multiple states, or CGT questions that don't have an obvious answer. A solicitor handles probate applications and contested matters, a conveyancer manages the title transfer itself, and a tax adviser works through CGT and estate tax calculations.

**Pro Tip:** *Order the title search before your first advice appointment and bring a copy. It saves the professional a step and often changes the advice you get.*

![When should you call a lawyer or tax adviser? — overview diagram](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787057089605_When-should-you-call-a-lawyer-or-tax-adviser-overview-diagram.jpeg)

## Where to check the official rules next

For details specific to your situation, go straight to primary sources rather than general articles.

- ATO co-ownership guidance for CGT rules on inherited shares.
- Your state or territory land titles office for transmission forms and identity checks.
- The probate office or Supreme Court registry for practice notes on grants.

## A funeral director's view on tenancy in common death

Families rarely think about property titles in the days after a death, and that's understandable. But the paperwork does not wait, and the biggest mistake I see is delay dressed up as grief. Executors who sit on the death certificate for weeks, assuming the property "sorts itself out," often find the mortgagee or a nervous co-owner forcing the pace later, on worse terms.

![Funeral director arranging folders on desk](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787056974146_Funeral-director-arranging-folders-on-desk.jpeg)

The conventional advice, "see a solicitor eventually," undersells how early the title search matters. Knowing whether you're dealing with tenants in common or joint tenancy changes everything about the weeks ahead, including whether probate is even needed for that asset. I'd rather a family spend $50 on a title search in the first fortnight than discover six months in that a step-sibling now owns a third of the family home.

Prioritise the practical over the emotional groundwork, at least for property. Confirm ownership, secure the documents, and get professional advice moving before decisions about the property get tangled up with decisions about the funeral and the family's grief. Working through how a Will shapes decisions alongside the property questions tends to bring clarity faster than either one alone.

If your family is navigating a death alongside funeral arrangements, Willow Tree Funerals can walk you through the practical next steps while you sort out the property side with your solicitor. Bruce Missen answers every call personally, 24 hours a day, and can help coordinate timing between the funeral and the estate administration. For families arranging services in the Manly area, visit our [funeral director Manly](https://willowtreefunerals.com.au/funeral-director-manly) page, or call 02 8776 1667 to speak with Bruce directly about what needs to happen next.

This article is general information, not a substitute for advice from a qualified lawyer. Consult a qualified legal professional about your own circumstances before acting on anything here.

## Sources

- [Co-ownership and right of survivorship](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/inherited-assets-and-capital-gains-tax/co-ownership-and-right-of-survivorship)
- [Change ownership following a death | Land Services](https://www.landservices.com.au/land-registration/change-ownership-following-a-death/)
- [What happens to property when a co-owner dies? - HQF Lawyers](https://hqf.com.au/what-happens-to-property-when-co-owner-dies/)
- [Joint Tenancy vs Tenants in Common](https://www.aussie.com.au/insights/articles/joint-tenants-tenants-in-common-difference/)

## FAQ

### What happens to a property when a tenant in common dies?

Their share becomes part of the deceased estate and passes under the Will, or under intestacy rules if there is no valid Will, rather than transferring automatically to the surviving co-owner.

### What are the dangers of tenants in common?

The main risk is that a co-owner's share can end up with beneficiaries you never expected to co-own with, such as a deceased partner's children, creating disputes over sale, buy-out, or continued use of the property.

### What is the 2-year rule for inherited property?

This refers to a common misconception around the main residence CGT exemption timeframe for inherited property; the actual rules depend on specific factors like the deceased's residency history and how the property has been used since, so check the ATO's guidance or a tax adviser for your exact situation.

### Does a surviving co-owner automatically inherit the whole property?

No. Only joint tenants have that automatic right of survivorship; tenants in common each hold a distinct share that passes through the deceased's estate to whoever the Will or intestacy law names.

### Do I need a solicitor to transfer a tenancy in common share after death?

Not always for a simple, uncontested estate, but a solicitor or conveyancer becomes essential once a mortgage discharge, a contested Will, or multi-state assets are involved.

## Recommended

- [Residuary estate in a will: what you need to know](https://blog.willowtreefunerals.com.au/blog/definition-of-residuary-estate)
- [Residue of estate: what executors and beneficiaries need to know](https://blog.willowtreefunerals.com.au/blog/residue-of-estate)
- [Next of kin in Australia: what it means and what it doesn't](https://blog.willowtreefunerals.com.au/blog/next-of-kin-what-does-it-mean)

title: Where to read Obama's eulogy in full, speech by speech
excerpt: Explore the full texts of Barack Obama's most memorable eulogies, available from reliable sources. Read, study, and reflect on his powerful speeches.
content:
![Empty funeral chapel pulpit ready for eulogy](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787117925463_Empty-funeral-chapel-pulpit-ready-for-eulogy.jpeg)

The full text of Barack Obama's major eulogies sits in three reliable places: official presidential archives, the Obama Foundation's own publishing channels, and major news outlets that transcribed each address at the time it was delivered. If you want to read or study his funeral speeches properly, four stand above the rest.

- **Senator Edward (Ted) Kennedy, 2009** — [Govinfo](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900669/pdf/DCPD-200900669.pdf)
- **Reverend Clementa Pinckney, 2015** — [White House archive transcript](https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2015/06/26/remarks-president-eulogy-honorable-reverend-clementa-pinckney)
- **Senator John McCain, 2018** — [The New York Times transcript](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/01/us/politics/barack-obama-john-mccain-funeral-eulogy.html)
- **Congressman John Lewis, 2020** — [Obama's own account on Medium](https://barackobama.medium.com/my-eulogy-for-congressman-john-lewis-101ea5eb49d1)

**Pro Tip:** *When a government archive or Obama's own channel has published the text, treat that as your primary source for citation. News outlet transcripts are excellent for cross-checking wording, but the archival or first-party version is what researchers and students should quote from.*

## Table of Contents

- [Obama's eulogy for Edward (Ted) Kennedy](#obamas-eulogy-for-edward-ted-kennedy)
- [Obama's eulogy for John Lewis](#obamas-eulogy-for-john-lewis)
- [Obama's eulogy for John McCain](#obamas-eulogy-for-john-mccain)
- [Obama's eulogy for Reverend Clementa Pinckney](#obamas-eulogy-for-reverend-clementa-pinckney)
- [Where to find authoritative transcripts, audio and video](#where-to-find-authoritative-transcripts-audio-and-video)
- [How to cite or study these speeches properly](#how-to-cite-or-study-these-speeches-properly)
- [A funeral director's note on why the full text matters](#a-funeral-directors-note-on-why-the-full-text-matters)
- [Sources](#sources)
- [FAQ](#faq)

## Obama's eulogy for Edward (Ted) Kennedy

Obama delivered this eulogy on 29 August 2009 at the Basilica of Our Lady of Perpetual Help in Boston, four days after Kennedy died of brain cancer. Kennedy had endorsed Obama during the bruising 2008 primary against Hillary Clinton, and the two men had worked together on healthcare reform for years. That relationship shaped the eulogy's warmth and its focus on Kennedy's decades in the Senate.

The official transcript is published through govinfo as a government record, and [NPR also carries the full text](https://www.npr.org/2009/08/29/112368135/text-president-obamas-eulogy-for-sen-kennedy) for readers who prefer a news-site copy. Both versions match closely, which makes this one of the easiest speeches to verify.

- Kennedy's 46 years in the Senate and his role in landmark legislation on civil rights, healthcare, and education
- Obama's personal debt to Kennedy for his early campaign support
- The rhetorical choice to present Kennedy as flawed and fully human, not sanitised in death

That last point is what makes the speech worth studying closely. The White House's own reflection on the address notes that its power comes from refusing to enlarge Kennedy into something he wasn't, choosing instead to describe an authentically human life. Obama leaned into that idea directly:

C-SPAN's video archive holds footage of the full funeral Mass if you want to hear the delivery alongside the written page.

## Obama's eulogy for John Lewis

Obama eulogised Congressman John Lewis on 30 July 2020 at Ebenezer Baptist Church in Atlanta, the pulpit once led by Martin Luther King Jr. Lewis had marched at Selma, been beaten on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, and served more than three decades in Congress. Obama's presence at the pulpit carried its own historical weight, and the eulogy is one of the few in this list to double as a direct legislative appeal.

Obama published the full text himself on Medium, which makes it the clearest primary source available. [CNN's full transcript](https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/30/politics/barack-obama-john-lewis-eulogy-full-transcript) is a solid secondary copy if you want to compare wording against the delivered version, and The New York Times also carried the remarks in full.

The eulogy moves well past tribute into advocacy. Obama used the platform to press Congress to pass what he called on lawmakers to name after Lewis:

That structure, tribute building toward a concrete ask, is what scholars and journalists return to when they study this speech. Video of the full service is available through Ebenezer Baptist Church's own recordings and several major network archives.

## Obama's eulogy for John McCain

Obama spoke at Washington National Cathedral in 2018 for Senator John McCain, a man who had run against him for the presidency a decade earlier and openly criticised him from the opposite side of politics for years afterward. McCain requested Obama as one of his eulogists before he died, which gives the speech an unusual frame: praise delivered across a genuine and lasting political divide.

- The New York Times published the full prepared remarks, the most widely cited transcript of this eulogy
- The National Cathedral's own video archive and several network news libraries carry footage of the full service
- Obama's remarks are frequently studied for how they turn McCain's stubbornness and contrarianism into virtues rather than flaws

Obama didn't smooth over the disagreements between them. He named them, then used that honesty to make the tribute land harder:

If you're analysing tone rather than just reading for content, this is the eulogy to compare against the Kennedy address. One leans on decades of friendship; the other builds its authority from respectful disagreement.

## Obama's eulogy for Reverend Clementa Pinckney

Obama delivered this eulogy on 26 June 2015, nine days after a gunman murdered Pinckney and eight members of his congregation during Bible study at Mother Emanuel AME Church in Charleston. Pinckney was both a pastor and a South Carolina state senator, and the eulogy was delivered against the raw backdrop of the massacre rather than natural death or long illness.

![Church altar with candles and hymnals](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787117914730_Church-altar-with-candles-and-hymnals.jpeg)

The full transcript is preserved on the official White House archive, which remains the authoritative version to cite. Major outlets republished it at the time, but the archived White House text is the one to reference for accuracy.

This is the most overtly moral of the four speeches, built around the concept of grace and what a community owes the dead beyond mourning. Obama pushed the congregation toward action rather than sentiment alone:

C-SPAN's archive carries the full video of the service, including the moment Obama led the congregation in singing "Amazing Grace."

## Where to find authoritative transcripts, audio and video

Not every copy of a presidential eulogy online is equally trustworthy, and the difference matters if you're citing one in an essay or a tribute.

- **Presidential archives and govinfo** hold the official government record, including "as delivered" remarks logged by the White House press office
- **The American Presidency Project** at UC Santa Barbara maintains a searchable database of presidential remarks going back decades
- **Obama's own channels**, particularly Medium, publish his personal account of a speech, which is as close to primary as it gets for the Lewis eulogy
- **Major outlets** like The New York Times, CNN, and NPR republish full transcripts, useful for cross-checking but technically secondary sources

**Pro Tip:** *Check three things before you trust a transcript: the publisher (government archive beats a random blog), the date stamp matching the actual delivery date, and whether the text is labelled "as delivered" rather than "prepared remarks" — the two can differ in small but meaningful ways.* For recordings, C-SPAN's archive and the relevant network's own YouTube channel are usually the most complete video sources, and lining up timestamps against the transcript is the fastest way to catch what was cut or added on the day.

## How to cite or study these speeches properly

For academic work, cite the speaker, the title of the remarks, the venue, the date, and the URL of the primary source. A workable format:

1. Obama, Barack. "Remarks in Eulogy for Reverend Clementa Pinckney." Charleston, SC, 26 June 2015. obamawhitehouse.archives.gov.
2. Use the news outlet transcript (NYT, CNN, NPR) as supporting material if the primary source is hard to access, noting it as a secondary citation.

For closer study, compare the written transcript against the video. Differences in pause, emphasis, or an ad-libbed line often reveal what Obama changed in the room versus what was on the page. Reading each speech's structure, personal connection, then public record, then a closing image or call to action, is a useful lens for tracking rhetorical choices across all four eulogies.

## A funeral director's note on why the full text matters

Families sometimes ask me for a line to read at a service, and I always point them to the full speech first, not just the excerpt doing the rounds online. Context changes meaning. Reading the whole Pinckney or Kennedy eulogy shows how a single line earned its weight.

**Pro Tip:** *If you're preparing a tribute, don't attempt to read an entire presidential eulogy word for word. Choose one short, honest passage and practise it aloud, with real pauses, rather than performing the whole text.* Always credit the original speaker and occasion when you borrow from it.

## Sources

For readers who want a shortlist to bookmark, these cover transcripts, government records, and recordings in one place.

- [Remarks by the President in Eulogy for the Honorable Reverend Clementa Pinckney | whitehouse.gov](https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2015/06/26/remarks-president-eulogy-honorable-reverend-clementa-pinckney)
- [My Eulogy for Congressman John Lewis | Medium](https://barackobama.medium.com/my-eulogy-for-congressman-john-lewis-101ea5eb49d1)

- [TRANSCRIPT: Barack Obama’s full eulogy of John Lewis | CNN Politics](https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/30/politics/barack-obama-john-lewis-eulogy-full-transcript)

## FAQ

### Who did Obama give a eulogy for?

Obama's most studied eulogies were for Senator Edward Kennedy (2009), Reverend Clementa Pinckney (2015), Senator John McCain (2018), and Congressman John Lewis (2020), each delivered at a funeral or memorial service tied to that person's public legacy.

![Timeline of Obama’s major eulogies](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787117907413_Timeline-of-Obama-s-major-eulogies.jpeg)

### What was Barack Obama's famous speech?

Beyond his eulogies, Obama is best known for major speeches outside of funerals, but among funeral speeches, the Pinckney and Lewis eulogies are the most widely cited.

### What is the most famous eulogy?

Among Obama's funeral addresses, the eulogy for Reverend Clementa Pinckney is often ranked as the most memorable, largely because of its moral framing around the Charleston church massacre and its closing rendition of "Amazing Grace."

### What was Obama's farewell speech?

Obama's farewell address, delivered in Chicago near the end of his presidency, was a presidential exit speech rather than a eulogy, reflecting on his two terms and urging citizens to stay engaged in democratic life.

If you're planning a service and want guidance on incorporating a meaningful reading, [Willow Tree Funerals](https://willowtreefunerals.com.au/pre-arrange) can help you shape a tribute that fits the moment, whether that's a full ceremony or a quiet graveside reading.

title: Philosophical death quotes to read now for comfort
excerpt: Explore ten thought-provoking philosophical death quotes that offer comfort and inspire a deeper understanding of life and mortality.
content:
![Calm funeral home sitting room with candlelight](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787349951168_Calm-funeral-home-sitting-room-with-candlelight.jpeg)

Here are ten philosophical death quotes to read now, each with a one-line note on what it offers.

1. **Marcus Aurelius**, *Meditations*: "You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do and say and think." A daily nudge to live with intention.
2. **Seneca**, *Letters from a Stoic*: "It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it." A rebuke to procrastination, not a threat.
3. **Epicurus**, *Letter to Menoeceus*: "Death is nothing to us." A logical case for releasing fear.
4. **Socrates**, as recorded by Plato: "No one knows whether death may not be the greatest good that can happen to a man." Comfort in uncertainty itself.
5. **Carl Jung**: "The idea of death... helps the soul towards its integration." Death as a psychological turning point.
6. **Buddha**, traditional teaching: "All that is mine, beloved and pleasant, will become otherwise, will become separated from me." Acceptance through impermanence.
7. **Alan Watts**: "The meaning of life is just to be alive." A modern call to presence.

**Pro Tip:** *Save the quote that unsettles you most; it usually points to the exercise your mind actually needs.*

## Key Takeaways

Reflecting on death through carefully chosen philosophical quotes, whether Stoic, existential or Buddhist, tends to ease fear and sharpen appreciation for life rather than deepen distress.

| Point | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Start with a shortlist | Keep ten or so quotes on hand across traditions so you have the right tone for any moment. |
| Match format to setting | Use short single lines for eulogies and longer passages for private journalling. |
| Practise, don't just read | Try memento mori or negative visualisation as a repeatable exercise, not a one-off quote. |
| Reflection has support | Mortality writing prompts produced a measurable six-day lift in positive language in controlled research. |
| Watch for real distress | Seek a counsellor or GP if reflection tips into ongoing anxiety rather than insight. |

## Table of Contents

- [Stoic and classical quotes on death from Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, Epicurus and Socrates](#stoic-and-classical-quotes-on-death-from-marcus-aurelius-seneca-epicurus-and-socrates)
- [Existential and modern reflections from Jung, Heidegger, Sartre, Alan Watts and Buddhist teaching](#existential-and-modern-reflections-from-jung-heidegger-sartre-alan-watts-and-buddhist-teaching)
- [How to use these quotes in reflection, eulogies and journalling](#how-to-use-these-quotes-in-reflection-eulogies-and-journalling)
- [Why reflecting on death with quotes helps, according to research](#why-reflecting-on-death-with-quotes-helps-according-to-research)
- [A funeral director's note on choosing words that comfort](#a-funeral-directors-note-on-choosing-words-that-comfort)
- [Why the standard advice on death quotes misses the point](#why-the-standard-advice-on-death-quotes-misses-the-point)
- [Sources](#sources)
- [FAQ](#faq)

## Stoic and classical quotes on death from Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, Epicurus and Socrates

The Stoics didn't write about death to frighten anyone. They wrote about it as a training tool, a way of stripping away the trivial so a person could focus on what mattered while they were still breathing. That's the thread running through every quote below.

- **Marcus Aurelius**: "Think of yourself as dead. You have lived your life. Now take what's left and live it properly." This is *memento mori* in its bluntest form, a Stoic exercise designed to reset priorities, not to induce dread.
- **Marcus Aurelius**: "Nature, which governs the whole, will soon change all things which you see, and out of their substance will make other things." Death here is recast as transformation, not ending.
- **Seneca**: "Let us prepare our minds as if we'd come to the very end of life." Seneca practised negative visualisation, imagining loss in advance to blunt its sting later.
- **Seneca**: "He who has learned to die has unlearned slavery." Freedom, for Seneca, started with accepting mortality.
- **Epicurus**: "So death, the most terrifying of ills, is nothing to us, since so long as we exist, death is not with us; but when death comes, then we do not exist." This is the symmetry argument in miniature: you were absent before birth and will be absent after death, so neither state can harm the person who is not there to experience it.
- **Socrates**, on trial for his life, reasoned that death is either a dreamless sleep or a passage to something better, and neither outcome warranted fear. His calm in the *Phaedo* remains one of philosophy's most cited consolations.

Two practices sit underneath these lines. *Memento mori* (Latin for "remember you will die") is the discipline of keeping mortality visible, often through a physical reminder or a daily reflection. Negative visualisation is its companion practice: deliberately imagining the loss of something valued, so gratitude replaces complacency when it's still yours. [Modern Stoic commentary](https://donaldrobertson.name/2014/10/10/the-contemplation-of-death-sample-chapter-from-teach-yourself-stoicism-2014/) notes both were meant to be practised often, not just recalled in a crisis, and researchers have found the same exposure logic underpins [cognitive behavioural approaches to death anxiety](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44202-022-00023-9) used today.

**Pro Tip:** *Try Seneca's exercise literally: each evening, spend sixty seconds imagining today was your last, then write one line about what you'd change tomorrow.*

![Hand lighting candle at funeral altar](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787349966272_Hand-lighting-candle-at-funeral-altar.jpeg)

## Existential and modern reflections from Jung, Heidegger, Sartre, Alan Watts and Buddhist teaching

Where the Stoics train the will, the existentialists interrogate meaning. Their quotes on mortality don't ask you to accept death calmly. They ask what death reveals about how you're living right now.

- **Carl Jung**: "Thoughts of death... prove on closer investigation to be fraught with meaning." Jung treated mortality as a psychological catalyst, arguing in his later writing that confronting death pushes the psyche toward integration rather than despair.
- **Martin Heidegger**: "Death is not an event in life. It is not a fact of the world." For Heidegger, awareness of death (what he called "being-towards-death") is what makes an authentic life possible, because it forces a person to stop living as everyone else expects.
- **Jean-Paul Sartre**: "It is the fact of my death which will decide the meaning of my life." Sartre's existentialism placed the responsibility for meaning squarely on the individual, with death as the deadline that gives choices their weight.
- **Alan Watts**: "You are under no obligation to be the same person you were five minutes ago." Watts pulled from Zen Buddhism to argue that clinging to a fixed self is what makes death terrifying, not death itself.
- **Buddhist teaching** on impermanence: attachment to permanence, not death, is the root of suffering. Letting go of the illusion that anything (including the self) is fixed is the practice, not a resignation to loss.

The difference from Stoicism is one of emphasis. Stoic quotes calm the mind by minimising death's importance; existential and Buddhist quotes lean the other way, treating death as the very thing that makes life, choice and identity meaningful in the first place.

A relatable example: someone grieving a parent might find Marcus Aurelius's line about impermanence a little cold in the raw first weeks. Sartre's framing, that the parent's choices only had meaning because their time was finite, can land differently. It doesn't ask for detachment. It asks the grieving person to notice what their parent actually built with limited time, which is often a gentler door into grief than a lesson in acceptance.

![Silhouetted tree branches with fading leaves at twilight](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787349959921_Silhouetted-tree-branches-with-fading-leaves-at-twilight.jpeg)

## How to use these quotes in reflection, eulogies and journalling

A quote lands differently depending on where you put it, so match the format to the moment.

1. **For a eulogy or funeral reading**, choose one short, plainly attributed line rather than a long passage. A single sentence from Marcus Aurelius or Socrates reads well aloud and doesn't ask a grieving room to follow dense argument.
2. **For private journalling**, longer passages work better. Copy out the full Epicurus symmetry argument or a Jung paragraph, then write for five minutes on what unsettles or reassures you about it.
3. **For a short meditation**, pick one line, read it slowly three times, then sit in silence for two minutes before writing a single sentence about what came up.
4. **For matching tone to belief**, Buddhist and Stoic lines tend to sit comfortably alongside most secular or multi-faith services, while overtly existentialist quotes (Sartre in particular) can feel jarring in a religious setting unless the family has specifically asked for a philosophical, non-religious tone.

**Pro Tip:** *If you're choosing a reading for someone else's service, ask a family member what the person actually believed about death. A quote that reflects the deceased's own outlook comforts a room far more than one that simply sounds profound.*

## Why reflecting on death with quotes helps, according to research

Sitting with mortality on purpose, rather than avoiding it, has a measurable effect. A [2014 study on mortality writing prompts](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265128916_More_than_words_Contemplating_death_enhances_positive_emotional_word_use) found that participants who wrote about their own death used more positive emotional language for six days afterwards. The reflection didn't sink mood. It lifted it.

Qualitative interviews back this up. People who deliberately confront their own finitude, through conversation, spiritual reflection or forward planning, often report [greater self-determination, dignity and psychosocial well-being](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9050349/) as a result. Separate research into art-based death meditation found the effect can last: participants showed sustained life appreciation for up to two weeks after a single guided session.

- Structured reflection (a quote, a prompt, a short meditation) appears more useful than avoidance.
- Effects vary by context and frequency of practice, so a one-off reading may do less than a regular five-minute habit.
- If contemplating death brings on real distress rather than reflection, that's a signal to talk to a counsellor or GP rather than push through alone.

## A funeral director's note on choosing words that comfort

> Families often ask me to help pick a reading that says what they can't quite put into words themselves. The right philosophical line doesn't need to explain grief away. It just needs to sound like something the person who died would have nodded along to.

My practical suggestion: soften a philosophical quote for a funeral service by trimming it to its clearest sentence, and pairing it with one line about why the family chose it. If you'd like help matching a quote to the tone of a Catholic, multi-faith or secular service, [Willow Tree Funerals](https://willowtreefunerals.com.au/services/catholic-funerals) can talk it through with you directly.

*— Bruce Missen, Willow Tree Funerals*

![Funeral director’s hands arranging floral wreath](https://csuxjmfbwmkxiegfpljm.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/blog-images/organization-6784/1787349958074_Funeral-director-s-hands-arranging-floral-wreath.jpeg)

## Why the standard advice on death quotes misses the point

Most lists of death quotes are sorted for prettiness, not use. That's the gap this list tries to close: a Stoic line for someone who needs their fear reduced, a Jung or Sartre line for someone who needs meaning restored, a Buddhist line for someone drowning in "why did this happen." Matching the quote to the actual psychological job it needs to do matters more than finding the most quotable sentence.

The conventional advice, pick something moving, undersells how much tone matching affects a grieving family. A line that sounds wise in an anthology can feel wrong read aloud in a chapel. My view, formed from watching families choose readings for years, is that the best quote is rarely the most famous one. It's the one that sounds like the person who died would have said it themselves.

If you're choosing for someone else, ask what they believed, not what sounds profound to you; memorial keepsakes can preserve such meaningful quotations for family reflection, as explained in this [family guide to memorial keepsake services](https://indianlifememorial.com/blog/what-is-a-memorial-keepsake-service-a-family-guide). If you're choosing for yourself, pick the quote that makes you slightly uncomfortable. That discomfort is usually where the useful reflection is hiding, and documenting the choice now saves your family a hard decision later.

## Sources

- [More than words: Contemplating death enhances positive emotional word use](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265128916_More_than_words_Contemplating_death_enhances_positive_emotional_word_use)
- [“My life became more meaningful”: confronting one’s own end of life and its effects on well‑being—a qualitative study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9050349/)

## FAQ

### What does Carl Jung say about death?

Jung argued that thoughts of death are "fraught with meaning" and that engaging with mortality, rather than avoiding it, helps the psyche move toward integration and wholeness in later life.

### What did Socrates say about dying?

At his trial, Socrates reasoned that death is either a dreamless, painless sleep or a passage to something better, and concluded no one truly knows whether "death may not be the greatest good that can happen to a man."

### What is a famous Stoic saying about death?

Marcus Aurelius's line "You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do and say and think" is among the most quoted Stoic reflections, used as a daily memento mori practice.

### What is a famous death quote overall?

Epicurus's line "Death is nothing to us" is one of the most cited philosophical quotes on mortality, built on the argument that a person can never actually experience being dead.

### Can reflecting on death actually make me feel better, not worse?

Research on mortality writing prompts found participants used more positive emotional language for six days afterwards, and separate studies on death meditation found increased life appreciation lasting up to two weeks, though effects vary and ongoing distress warrants professional support.

## Recommended

- [Fear of death quotes: comfort and guidance for Sydney families](https://blog.willowtreefunerals.com.au/blog/fear-of-death-quotes)
- [The bargaining stage of grief: what it looks like and how to cope](https://blog.willowtreefunerals.com.au/blog/stage-of-bargaining)
- [Telling family your funeral preferences: a practical guide](https://blog.willowtreefunerals.com.au/blog/telling-family-your-funeral-preferences-a-practical-guide)
